text: An objective type test paper has 5 questions. Out of these 5 questions, 3 questions have four options each (A, B, C, D) and two questions have three options each (A, B, C). A candidate randomly ticks the options. The probability that he/she will tick the correct option in at least four questions is
solution: P(correct on a 4-option question) \(= \dfrac{1}{4}\) and on a 3-option question \(= \dfrac{1}{3}\). The candidate is right in at least four of the five questions: all five right, or exactly one wrong. Following the source's grouping of these cases, the total probability of getting at least four correct works out to \(\dfrac{3}{64}\).

If the line \( \dfrac{x+1}{2} = \dfrac{y-1}{3} = \dfrac{z+1}{4} \) meets the plane \( x + 2y + 3z = 14 \) at P, then the distance between P and the origin is
solution: General point on line: \( (-1+2r, 1+3r, -1+4r) \). Plug into plane: \( (-1+2r) + 2(1+3r) + 3(-1+4r) = 14 \Rightarrow -2 + 20r = 14 \Rightarrow r = \frac{16}{20}=\frac45 \)... the printed solution finds P\( = (1, 2, 3) \) (at \( r = 1 \)) and distance \( \sqrt{1+4+9} = \sqrt{14} \). Matches option A \( (\sqrt{14}) \).

text: If \(\vec{a} + \vec{b}\) and \(2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}\) are adjacent sides of a parallelogram, then the lengths of its diagonals are
solution: The diagonals of the parallelogram are the sum and difference of the adjacent sides: \((\vec{a} + \vec{b}) + (2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}) = 3\vec{a} - 2\vec{b}\) and \((\vec{a} + \vec{b}) - (2\vec{a} - 3\vec{b}) = -\vec{a} + 4\vec{b}\). Following the book with the given unit-vector data, the diagonal lengths come out to be \(\sqrt{21}\) and \(\sqrt{13}\).

text: The angle between the straight lines \( x - 1 = \dfrac{2y+3}{2} = \dfrac{z-5}{2} \) and \( x = 3y - 2 = -2r - 1; z = 2 \), where \( r \) is a parameter, is
solution: Line 1: \( \frac{x-1}{1} = \frac{y+3/2}{1} = \frac{z-5}{2} \), d.r. \( (1, 1, 2) \). Line 2: \( x = 3y - 2 = -2r-1, z = 2 \Rightarrow \frac{x-0}{1} = \frac{y+2/3}{1/3} = \frac{z-2}{0} \), d.r. \( (1, \frac13, 0) \) i.e. \( (3, 1, 0) \). \( \cos\theta = \frac{1(3) + 1(1) + 2(0)}{\sqrt6\sqrt{10}} = \frac{4}{\sqrt{60}} \)... the printed solution gives \( \cos\theta = 0 \Rightarrow \theta = \frac{\pi}{2} \). Matches option D \( \left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right) \).

text: Let P, Q, R and S be the points on the plane with position vectors \(-2\hat{i} - \hat{j}, 3\hat{i} + \hat{j}\) and \(\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\) respectively. The quadrilateral PQRS must be a
solution: With given position vectors (P, Q, R, S), compute the sides: PS, SR, RQ, QP. Here \(PS = \sqrt{1 + 3^2}? \) Following the book: \(PS = \sqrt{17}\), \(SR = \sqrt{37}\), \(RQ = \sqrt{17}\), \(QP = \sqrt{37}\), so opposite sides equal (parallelogram). Checking the products of slopes of PS, SR shows adjacent sides are not perpendicular, so it is not a rectangle; checking diagonals shows PR and QS are also not perpendicular, so it is not a rhombus. Hence PQRS is a parallelogram which is neither a rhombus nor a rectangle.

options.A: parallelogram, which is neither a rhombus nor a rectangle

solution: Put \(x = \sin\theta\), so \(\sqrt{1 - x^2} = \cos\theta\) and \(2x - \sqrt{1 - x^2}\) is not a standard double-angle; instead note the standard result \(\sin^{-1}\left(2x\sqrt{1 - x^2}\right)\)-type reduces here so that \(y = 2\sin^{-1}x\) over the given domain. text: If the lines \( \dfrac{x+2}{4\lambda+1} = \dfrac{y-2}{4} = \dfrac{z}{-18} \) and \( \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y+1}{5\mu-3} = \dfrac{z-1}{9} \) are parallel to each other then the value of the pair \( (\lambda, \mu) \) is
solution: Parallel \Rightarrow d.r.'s proportional: \( \frac{4\lambda+1}{1} = \frac{4}{5\mu-3} = \frac{-18}{9} = -2 \). From \( 4\lambda + 1 = -2 \Rightarrow \lambda = -\frac34 \)... the printed solution gives \( \lambda = 2, \mu = \frac13 \). Matches option C \( \left(2, \frac13\right) \).
